items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: But, so they collaborated, that is Buck Clayton and Li Jinhui, and created this fusion of Chinese music and jazz.

ctx.x: He was in Shanghai in 1935 with his group, the Harlem Gentlemen, even though he was from Los Angeles. And that was because Duke Ellington was big during the advent of radio in the 1930’s, so in China they heard Duke Ellington, and so Buck Clayton took advantage of Ellington’s power, of his music, it was in New York, and called it the Harlem Gentlemen rather than Los Angeles.
